The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple, decentralized model of language origins, based on the principles of motor, perceptual, and cognitive realism, can account for the emergence of complex syllable systems.

the syllable system of human languages may have emerged from a process that is both natural (in the sense of not requiring any external intervention) and universal (in the sense that it applies to all societies of agents endowed with the appropriate apparatus).
the syllabic structure of human language is not a unique and exceptional trait of the human species.
